questions.q: In a collision, what is the "remote update"?
options: The version of the record already sitting on the target instance
The incoming change captured in the Update Set being promoted
A record that has no version on either instance
A record that was deleted on the target instance
questions.explain: The remote update is the incoming change from the Update Set; the local update is what's already on the target.

questions.q: What are the three legitimate outcomes once you review a collision's remote and local versions side by side?
options: Delete both versions, restart the Update Set, or escalate to the vendor
Keep the remote version, keep the local version, or manually reconcile both into a corrected version
Always keep remote, always keep local, or always skip the record
Ignore the collision, re-run the preview, or cancel the commit entirely
questions.explain: Those are the three real, deliberate decisions a reviewer can make after comparing remote and local versions.

questions.q: What is the real risk of blindly accepting the remote version on every collision without reviewing it?
options: It can silently overwrite a legitimate, intentional change someone made directly on the target instance
ServiceNow will automatically block the commit if remote is accepted too often
It always causes an immediate system outage
There is no real risk, since the Update Set always represents the correct version
questions.explain: A collision exists because the target changed after the Update Set was created — that change may be a legitimate fix the remote version would quietly erase.

questions.q: When is manual reconciliation the right call, instead of simply picking remote or local?
options: Only when the Update Set is empty
When the remote and local updates touch genuinely different aspects of the same record, and picking either side alone would lose real work from the other
Never — reconciliation is not a real option in ServiceNow
Only when the collision involves more than ten records at once
questions.explain: If the remote update fixes one part of a record and the local update fixes a different part, combining both avoids losing either change.

questions.q: What did course 3 already establish about collisions, that this lesson builds on rather than repeats?
options: The detailed field-by-field reconciliation workflow
That a collision happens when the target instance's version differs from what's in the Update Set
The exact steps for a partial commit recovery
How to batch Update Sets by feature
questions.explain: Course 3 covered the basic definition of a collision; this lesson goes deeper into the real review and resolution workflow.
